newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India GDRs follow strong Bombay higher.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India GDRs follow strong Bombay higher.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts posted strong gains on Wednesday in moderate trade following a rally in Bombay earlier, brokers and traders said.
They said prices had picked up after drifting lower for the first two days of the week, and expected local market strength to continue, aiding GDR prices.
"We had been expecting a consolidation, but that has not happened and the market still has momentum," said a broker.
He said the local market's run had not been checked by the sort of selling pressure that had stalled earlier rallies.
Reliance extended Tuesday's gains to add 67 cents to $22.50/23.50, and SBI added $1.05 to $27.00/28.00. Hindalco was softer as sellers appeared, losing 67 cents to $34.25/35.25.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.83 points higher at 89.00, a 2.10 percent rise, with the premium over the local market at 19.89 percent from 19.00 percent.
Bombay's benchmark index added 98.30 points to 4,404.69.
The HSBC James Capel Korea GDR Index was softer after the local market struggled for gains earlier. The index shed 0.89 points to 76.33 points, a premium of 38.66 percent over the local market.

The Capel Taiwan GDR Index finished 2.82 points higher at 132.04, representing a discount to the local market of 1.77 percent. The local market's weighted index resumed gains on Wednesday despite expectations of a consolidation after Wall Street gained overnight.
